defects.claim: A subscriber reacting to the synchronous loading update reenters beginLoad before slot.load is set, which parses the source twice and publishes readiness twice
CFF2 outlines (font.tables.cff2) are reported as truetype by embeddingOf, which misroutes PDF and SVG font embedding
defects.scenario: a variable OpenType font with a `CFF2` table and no `glyf`. The parser accepts it (`checkCff` handles CFF2, and opentype.js reads it), but `outlines` is `'cff'` only when `t.cff` is set. If opentype.js stores a CFF2 Top DICT anywhere other than `tables.cff`, the embedding says `'truetype'`, so a PDF writer embeds it as a TrueType program with no `glyf` table and the glyphs come out blank. The check should be on the sfnt's own tables (`tableOf(sfnt, 'CFF ') ?? tableOf(sfnt, 'CFF2')`, as the parser already does). The `FaceEmbedding.outlines` doc ("a `CFF ` table and no `glyf`") is silent on CFF2. Not verified: opentype.js is not installed in this tree.
defects.cause: outline kind read from parser state rather than tables

defects.claim: GPOS reader's work budget never counts subtables, so a small GPOS can still hang or exhaust memory in pairSubtables
defects.scenario: The kern feature lists 65535 lookup indices (a 131 KB list). The LookupList has 65535 offsets, all pointing at one type-2 lookup whose subTableCount is 65535. `subtablesOf` is memoized by *index*, not by lookup offset, so every index walks and pushes all 65535 subtable offsets. That is ~4.3e9 reads and an array of ~4.3e9 numbers from a font of a few hundred KB, which is an OOM or hang during registration. After that, every `kernOf` call walks them all again. `workBudget` exists to stop exactly this case ("tables share one long list"), but `pairSubtables` never calls `spend`. It should charge `count` per lookup, or memoize by lookup offset so a shared lookup is walked once.
defects.cause: subtable walk outside the work budget

defects.claim: A .ttc whose member offsets all name one huge directory makes membersOf reread it per member, quadratic work on a damaged file
defects.scenario: A ttcf header has numFonts = 250 000 (1 MB of member offsets), and every offset names the same directory with numTables = 65535 (1 MB of records). `membersOf` calls `memberName` for every member, and each call builds the full 65535-record array just to find `name`. That is ~1.6e10 record objects from a 2 MB file, a hang inside `sfntFromCollection` before any parser runs. The `.dfont` path refuses a resource named twice for this reason ("cannot copy more than the file"), but the ttcf path does not dedupe directory offsets, and does not bound records × members. It could memoize by `dirOffset`, or refuse two members sharing a directory.
defects.cause: no dedupe of member directory offsets

defects.claim: checkCff does quadratic work when many FDArray Font DICTs share one Private DICT's Subrs INDEX, rereading it each time
defects.scenario: An FDArray INDEX holds 65535 small Font DICTs (~5 bytes each), each with a `Private` operator naming the same Private DICT, whose `Subrs` names one 65535-item INDEX (offSize 1 with zero-length items, ~64 KB). `readIndex` re-walks and re-allocates the 65535 items for every Font DICT: ~4.3e9 iterations from a CFF table of under 0.5 MB. The structural check meant to keep a damaged face from holding the thread becomes the hang. Checking each distinct `(at, size)` Private and each Subrs offset only once bounds it by the table size.
defects.cause: shared Private/Subrs re-read per Font DICT

defects.claim: The cmap and CFF checks read a different table than opentype.js parses when a tag is listed twice or a table's length runs past the file
defects.scenario: `tableOf` takes the first record with a tag, and returns null when `offset + length` runs past the file. opentype.js reads tables at their offset, ignores the length, and keeps the last record for `CFF `/`CFF2` and parses every `cmap` record. So (a) a truncated or damaged file whose `CFF ` or `cmap` record states an overlong length skips `checkCff`/`checkCmap` entirely, and opentype.js then parses the table from its offset; (b) a font listing `cmap` or `CFF ` twice has only the first copy checked. Either way the hang and heap blow-up the checks were written to refuse reach opentype.js. The same mismatch decides `glyf`/`loca` presence: an overlong `glyf` record makes the code treat a TrueType font as CFF. These should refuse a duplicate tag or out-of-file table, or check exactly what opentype.js will read.

defects.claim: Pairs kerned only under a language-specific LangSys get kerned in default text
defects.scenario: `lookupIndexSets` emits one set per LangSys: `latn` default, then each `latn` language system (e.g. `NLD `, `TRK `), then `DFLT`. `pairKerning` returns the first set that kerns the pair. A pair that `latn` default leaves unkerned but a language-specific LangSys kerns gets that language's adjustment in ordinary Latin text, which no shaper does. The doc comment calls the sets alternatives, but they are applied as a fallback chain. Language systems should come after every script's default LangSys, or be left out.

defects.claim: GPOS ScriptList records sharing one Script table multiply LangSys iteration past the work budget
defects.scenario: a GPOS whose ScriptList holds 65,535 records all pointing at one Script table with 65,535 LangSys records (~800 KB of tables). `langSysesOf` memoizes the Script table, so `spend(langSysCount)` is charged once, but `scripts` gets one entry per record sharing the same `langSysAt`, and the loop at line 149 walks all 65,535 × 65,535 ≈ 4.3e9 entries doing a `langSysSeen.has` each. The budget (4 per byte, ~3.2M here) never trips, and the face's load hangs for minutes. Dedupe `scripts` by Script table offset, or spend per record walked.
defects.cause: memoized table shared by records, iteration not budgeted

defects.claim: A WOFF's output buffer is sized from recorded table lengths, up to 1032× the file size, before any table is inflated
defects.scenario: a 2 MB WOFF whose compressed tables each record `origLength = 1032 × compLength`. The ratio check passes, and `new ArrayBuffer(size)` asks for ~2 GB before `inflateInto` can find that the streams decompress to far less. The allocation either fails (the face fails to load, which is fine) or succeeds and holds 2 GB through every `await` of the inflate loop in a tab. The header's `totalSfntSize` (offset 16) states the real size and is never compared, nor is the buffer grown as tables actually inflate.
